habitat: Usually in pairs in the middle layers of forest fringes.
summary: A fairly common resident. Dark brown above, with a white wing-bar and a black crest. The male has a black throat and breast. The female’s throat is finely spotted and her breast is mottled. The belly is white. The call is a rasping zwee-zwer, almost the same as the paradise flycatcher. The Kemp name Bluemantled Flycatcher and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Paradise Flycatcher has a blue bill and long central tail feathers in the male.

head.pattern: Crested black head. The throat is finely spotted.

viewNotes.note: Dark brown above, with a white wing-bar and a black crest, throat and breast.
Finely spotted throat and a mottled breast. White belly.
Whiter underparts than White-tailed Crested Flycatcher. The flight underside is not described separately.

calls.description: A rasping 'zwee-zwer', almost the same as African Paradise Flycatcher. The male also sings a high 'kwew-ew-ew-ew' followed by four clicks. The grade A call is from Port Alfred. The filename is XC416342-Blue-mantled Crested Flycatcher call.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape. The Kemp name Bluemantled Flycatcher and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 4–16.
